_meta.note: Two operator how-tos whose proofs are 'does the alarm actually go off?' negative tests of safety mechanisms we currently only watch pass. PR0: a parity self-test — inject a real node<->python divergence into a throwaway copy of the Python runtime (via a new HB_PY_SRC seam that leaves default behavior unchanged) and assert tests/parity.sh FLAGS it and names the diverging surface; today parity.sh is only ever seen to pass when equal, never proven to fail when it should. PR1: a recovery proof — drive the public hb CLI to corrupt state.json (doctor reports drift, rebuild heals), delete a completed gate's artifact (doctor reports rot), and confirm rebuild is idempotent. PR2: the two guides + index + a T55 group that enforces both demos so they cannot rot. Same dogfooded discipline: every claim a runnable proof, each phase refuted by a distinct actor.

tasks.title: Add a test seam to parity.sh
tasks.description: Add an HB_PY_SRC override to tests/parity.sh (default $ROOT/py/src; behavior unchanged) so a mutated copy of the Python runtime can be substituted — the seam that lets a divergence be injected without editing the real runtime. Verify tests/parity.sh still passes by default.

tasks.title: Write parity-selftest.sh
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/parity-selftest.sh: confirm baseline tests/parity.sh is green, then copy the Python runtime, inject a deliberate node<->python divergence (a phantom lint error), run tests/parity.sh against the mutated copy via HB_PY_SRC, and assert the harness FLAGS it (non-zero exit, a divergence marked on the lint surface). Print PARITY-SELFTEST-CAUGHT only when the alarm fires on the real harness.

tasks.title: Write recovery-demo.sh
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/recovery-demo.sh: via the public hb CLI stand up a project and complete a phase whose gate references an artifact, then exercise recovery — corrupt state.json and assert hb doctor reports the projection drift and hb rebuild heals it; delete the completed gate's artifact and assert hb doctor reports the rot ('no longer reproducible'); assert rebuild is idempotent (two rebuilds project identical state). Print RECOVERY-GUARDS-OK when all hold.

tasks.title: Write the two guides
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/keep-the-runtimes-in-parity.md (the parity contract, what a shared surface is, intentional divergences, and proving the alarm fires; proof: parity-selftest.sh) and docs/howto/recover-a-dead-or-corrupted-run.md (event-log-is-truth, rebuild, doctor rot/drift; proof: recovery-demo.sh). Follow the project doc rules; link AGENTS rules 1 and 2 and planning/parity-notes.md rather than restating them.

tasks.title: Index + enforce
tasks.description: Add both guides to docs/howto/README.md; add a T55 group to tests/run-tests.sh that runs parity-selftest.sh and recovery-demo.sh and asserts their markers, so the proofs cannot rot.

GATE_PR0.desc: parity.sh still passes by default, and a self-test proves it flags a real injected node<->python divergence.

review.prompt: Refute that PR0 is done: does the HB_PY_SRC seam leave default parity behavior unchanged (not silently weaken it)? Does parity-selftest.sh inject a REAL runtime divergence (not just make python crash, which would trip parity for the wrong reason)? Is the non-zero exit actually due to the divergence, on the lint surface, and would the selftest ESCAPE-report if parity failed to catch it? Could it pass vacuously?

criteria.desc: parity is green by default (seam unchanged behavior)
the self-test proves parity flags an injected divergence

GATE_PR1.desc: The recovery demo drives the real runtime: doctor detects drift and rot, and rebuild heals and is idempotent.

review.prompt: Refute that PR1 is done: does recovery-demo.sh drive the REAL hb CLI (not a mock)? Is each alarm load-bearing — would the drift check fail if state.json were NOT corrupted, and the rot check fail if the artifact were NOT deleted (so it is not asserting a constant)? Does rebuild actually heal (state matches the canonical projection), or does the demo pass vacuously?

GATE_PR2.desc: Each guide points at a proof that runs; the index lists both; the suite enforces the demos.

review.prompt: Refute that PR2 is done: does either guide claim a proof that does not run? Does either restate the enforced rules (AGENTS, parity-notes) rather than link them? Is either guide missing from the index? Does T55 actually run both demos and assert their markers?

criteria.desc: each guide references its runnable proof

criteria.cmd: for f in keep-the-runtimes-in-parity recover-a-dead-or-corrupted-run; do grep -q "$f" "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/howto/README.md" || exit 1; done

criteria.desc: the node suite enforces the demos (T55 group PASSED)
